name: Adoption

objectives.text: Identify that God makes people who trust in Jesus His own children
Recite the opening words of the Lord's Prayer and name God as the Father in heaven whom Jesus taught His people to address
Describe ways Jesus says the heavenly Father feeds, protects, and gives good gifts to His children
Explain what the words Abba, Father mean and where Paul uses them to describe how God's children may speak to Him
Recite and explain in their own words the catechism definition of adoption as God's free grace receiving sinners into His family with all its privileges
Describe how adoption makes believers brothers and sisters in one household of God and give examples of how Scripture calls them to treat one another
Explain what Romans 8:15-16 teaches about the Spirit of adoption bearing witness with the believer's spirit that they are children of God
Compare the standing of a slave with that of a son and heir as Paul and Jesus use these images to describe God's people
Compose a prayer that addresses God as Father following the pattern and boldness Scripture gives His children
Explain how Scripture calls God's adopted children to resemble their Father in love, mercy, and conduct
Explain how first-century Greco-Roman adoption practice illuminates Paul's use of the term adoption
Distinguish adoption from justification and regeneration by stating what each act of grace accomplishes for the sinner
Interpret what it means that believers are heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, including Paul's link between sharing His sufferings and sharing His glory
Identify the privileges of God's children listed in the Westminster Confession and match each to a supporting passage of Scripture
Explain how Hebrews 12 interprets the Lord's discipline of believers as evidence of fatherly love rather than punishment
Contrast Christ's eternal sonship by nature with believers' sonship by adoption and explain why the tradition insists on the difference
Trace the theme of God's sonship from Israel as God's firstborn son through the promises to David's heir to its fulfillment in Christ and the church
Construct a theology of adoption from Galatians 4:1-7 that accounts for the Father's timing, the Son's redemption, and the Spirit's witness
Analyze the already and not yet of adoption by comparing present sonship with the future adoption Paul links to the redemption of the body
Evaluate the claim of the universal fatherhood of God by distinguishing God as Creator of all people from God as Father of His adopted children
Explain the historical significance of the Westminster Confession devoting a separate chapter to adoption and assess what that choice contributes to Reformed teaching on salvation
Write a theological argument that defends adoption as a distinct grace of the gospel and shows its relationship to the other benefits of salvation

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (children of God, Our Father, Abba, catechism definition, Spirit of adoption, servant versus son, prayer, distinction from justification and regeneration, heirs, fatherly discipline, Galatians 4 theology, universal fatherhood, distinct grace). Dropped filler such as 'observe that God's children are loved' (replaced with a concrete description of fatherly care from Matthew), the vague 'highest privilege' synthesis, and the union-with-Christ link that belongs to a sibling sub-topic (refocused as Christ's natural sonship versus adopted sonship using Heidelberg Q33). Recast the prayer objective as composing a prayer rather than feeling confidence, and the Spirit's witness as explaining the text rather than experiencing assurance. Added missing competencies: household of God relationships, resembling the Father, Greco-Roman background, WCF 12.1 privileges with proofs, Old Testament sonship of Israel and David's heir, the future adoption of Romans 8:23, and the historical significance of WCF chapter 12. Replaced vague confession labels with exact numbered references and gave every scripture citation verses.
